text:
customer-success: Heads-up — BlueFin (EU) saw intermittent 429s since ~2026-02-12T00:12Z. Pattern: short bursts lasting 3–5m, roughly every ~60s. Customer says their client isn’t doing exponential backoff. Opening here for ENG triage. Ticket #34567

miranda: Thanks. Do we have an example request-id / api_key last4? Is traffic generation or embeddings? Any recent deploys in eu-west?

customer-success: Request sample and last4 sent to ticket: path=/v1/generate, api_key_last4=7b2c, region=eu-west-1, route=/v1/generate (chat/generation), mostly small prompts (50–200 tokens). No deploys reported.

raj: Quick look at logs — I can already see repeated 429s with Retry-After: 60. Headers from one failure:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1779994320
X-Account-TPM: 360000
X-Account-TPM-Remaining: 0
Request-ID: rq_8f3e2b
```

raj: That looks like both RPM (requests/min) and TPM (tokens/min) exhausted in those short windows. Could be many clients aligned or a cron/heartbeat.

sasha: Repro attempt (local): I ran a quick burst script to simulate 90 concurrent small generation requests in one second:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 90); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate &
done; wait
```

sasha: Within ~30s we saw 429s with the same headers. Suggests the account hit an RPM burst cap.

kevin: Quick checklist while we triage:
- confirm whether limits are account-wide or per-api-key (both matter).
- check for multiple keys from same customer hitting endpoints simultaneously.
- verify if embedding jobs are running in parallel (embeddings burn tokens fast).
- check client behaviour: fixed-interval retries vs exponential backoff.

miranda: Immediate mitigations to advise the customer:
- add jitter + exponential backoff (start 500ms, *2, cap ~30s).
- spread requests over time (avoid fan-in at minute boundaries).
- batch small requests where possible or use streaming to reduce request count.
- obey Retry-After header (do not hammer).

raj: Infra notes for ENG:
- look at per-route quota vs account quota. Route might have lower RPM.
- check our ingress proxies for short-term burst smoothing (we have a small token-bucket with burst allowance).
- look at whether our rate-limiter is counting websocket/stream opens as separate requests.

customer-success: Customer says their traffic pattern is many mobile clients that wake from background at top of minute and all sync. That would explain minute-aligned spikes.

miranda: Action plan:
1) I’ll ask CS to send mitigation steps to customer now (backoff + jitter + staggering).
2) Raj — can you pull per-key RPM/TPM graphs for the account + see if there are simultaneous keys?
3) If we confirm account-wide RPM exhaustion and customer is production-critical, propose a temporary quota uplift (soft increase) — will need support lead OK.

raj: On it. I pulled the dashboard: three keys from BlueFin active. Graph shows ~1.1k req/min sustained during spikes, tokens/min peaking at ~320k. The account default RPM=1000 and TPM=300k. So both hit at same windows.

ops-bot: <https://console.redwood.ai/accounts/bluefin/rate-limits|Rate-limit dashboard> — live view attached to ticket #34567. :mag:

kevin: If customer can’t quickly change client behaviour, recommend either Dedicated capacity (reserved RPM/TPM) or temporary quota bump while they implement backoff. Also suggest implementing client-side random jitter so device wakes don't align.

sasha: Small repro tip for support docs: recommend a one-liner stress test that mimics mobile wake-up pattern (burst of N requests every 60s) so customers can validate:
```bash
while true; do for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"tick"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate & done; wait; sleep 60; done
```

miranda: Raj — ETA on graphs & temp quota suggestion?

raj: I’ll prepare the graphs and a quota uplift proposal in 20m. If support lead approves, we can apply a 25% soft increase for 2 hours to keep customer online.

customer-success: I’ll relay to BlueFin now and recommend staggering client sync windows + implement backoff. They asked if there’s anything else to check on our side (clock skew, duplicate key usage?).

kevin: Add: confirm no upstream proxy is retransmitting requests and ensure mobile SDK doesn’t open repeated connections on network flaps. Also verify server time drift — but that's less common.

miranda: Good. I’ll leave this thread open. If we get repro in staging, we can suggest code snippets for SDKs. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
